name: menopause overview
title: Menopause: where she is in the transition (perimenopause, menopause, early menopause at 40 to 45, premature ovarian insufficiency under 40, each with its cycle and hormone cut-offs), then for hot flashes whether she can safely start menopausal hormone therapy (estrogen, plus progesterone if she has a uterus) or needs non-hormonal drugs, and for genitourinary symptoms local treatment in two steps

root.title: Menopause: where is she in the transition, and can she take menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) for her symptom?
lines: history: last menstrual period (LMP) · hot flashes, sleep, mood, genitourinary, libido · a blood clot or breast cancer?
abnormal or post-menopausal bleeding: see the ABNORMAL BLEEDING chart · bone: see the OSTEOPOROSIS chart

groups.title: WHERE IS SHE? set by her AGE and her LAST PERIOD
lines: the same symptoms at every stage; the periods are what differ

groups.title: HOT FLASHES: can she safely start MHT?
lines: everyone first: cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) · hypnosis · weight loss · cooling, avoid triggers
YES only if: NO contraindication AND < 60 AND < 10 years post menopause

groups.title: GENITOURINARY: treat it LOCALLY
lines: estrogen deficiency of the genitourinary tract

head: h
Perimenopause
'around menopause': periods not yet stopped
clue: symptoms can start MANY YEARS before the last period
inv: cycle lengths differ by ≥ 7 days, persistently
no period for ≥ 60 days · follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) > 25 IU/L
tx: Irregular bleeding makes it HARD to treat
heavy or irregular: see the ABNORMAL BLEEDING chart

head: h
Menopause
average age 51–52 in Canada
tx: Treat the symptom she wants treated
hot flashes → MHT or non-hormonal · genitourinary → local

head: h
Early menopause
menopause at 40–45
clue: coronary heart disease · stroke · cardiovascular + all-cause death

head: h
MHT: ESTROGEN
the gold standard for hot flashes
clue: yes → add PROGESTERONE · no → estrogen alone

head: h
NON-HORMONAL
clue: a contraindication · or ≥ 60 · or ≥ 10 years post menopause
inv: undiagnosed vaginal bleeding · breast cancer, ever
estrogen-dependent cancer · heart disease · clot or stroke, EVER · thrombophilia · liver disease · pregnancy
tx: fezolinetant · elinzanetant: calm the hot-flash neurons

head: h
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM)
clue: dryness, burning · dyspareunia, ↓ libido · urgency, dysuria, recurrent urinary tract infection
inv: rule out skin conditions · pale, thin · vaginal pH > 5.0
tx: avoid irritants · ↓ caffeine · regular sex · physiotherapy

panels.title: Nutrition for every woman in menopause
items: sodium < 1300 mg · vitamin D 800 IU · calcium 1200 mg
